claim: Placeholder: identify evidence-supported groups that materially legitimized or reproduced the pre/post-coup system and test whether perceived distribution or status worsened.
mechanism_to_next_layer: No transition from grievance to regime instability is assumed without evidence.
alternative_explanations: The relevant legitimacy-bearing groups may differ across military, civilian and regional institutions.

claim: Placeholder: assess status loss and expectation-reality gap among evidence-supported legitimacy-bearing groups.
mechanism_to_next_layer: Potential importance only if linked to trust, defection, mobilization, resistance or institutional behavior.
alternative_explanations: Status loss can produce adaptation rather than opposition.

claim: Placeholder: rainfall, drought, heat, floods, crop and environmental shocks relevant to local livelihoods.
mechanism_to_next_layer: Climate -> livelihood/water/food/migration pathway must be demonstrated.
alternative_explanations: Seasonal and regional variation may dominate national averages.

claim: Placeholder: staple-food prices, crop output, market access, transport and household affordability.
mechanism_to_next_layer: Food availability != affordability; local access mechanism required.
alternative_explanations: Conflict or pandemic effects may be confounded with pre-existing poverty.

claim: Placeholder: drinking/irrigation water access, seasonal scarcity, floods and infrastructure disruption.
mechanism_to_next_layer: Water stress only contributes through an evidenced social/economic mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Water conditions may be localized and unrelated to political dynamics.

claim: Placeholder: fuel availability, electricity, transport energy and affordability affecting households and logistics.
mechanism_to_next_layer: Fuel exists != fuel deliverable; logistics effects must be separated from household effects.
alternative_explanations: Energy stress may reflect broader economic disruption rather than independent pressure.
